correctness.rationale: Equation (1) is derived from the associative Nijenhuis identity for an arbitrary rank-one tensor. A nonzero functional forces the image generator to satisfy U^2=lambda U; c=f(U)=0 is precisely the weight-zero Rota–Baxter condition, and the Rota–Baxter identity itself forces c=0 using X=U,Y=I. If c!=0 the kernel of f is a codimension-one subalgebra. Trace pairing identifies its product bilinear form with left multiplication by F, giving n rank(F)<=2 and hence n=2 with rank F=1. Simplicity forces f(I)=0, so F^2=0; conjugating F to E_12 reduces the Nijenhuis identity to Cayley–Hamilton det(U)=0. The converse is verified. The exception count divides the exact number of admissible nonzero (F,U) presentations by q-1. The complementary Rota–Baxter count is independently derived by nilpotent and idempotent projective image-generator cases. The package checker enumerates all rank-one maps over GF(2), GF(3), GF(4) via their unique normalized image generators, testing 16 basis-pair identities per map; observed (RB,N,exception) counts are (15,27,12), (56,128,72), (135,375,240). These finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-fields threshold between rank-one associative Nijenhuis and weight-zero Rota–Baxter maps, the normal form of its non-Rota–Baxter exceptions, and the finite-field exceptional census were compared against the relevant primary theory, the closest available prior matrix-algebra rank-one Rota–Baxter classification, and scientific publication-record searches. The closest prior matrix result classifies only Rota–Baxter maps and therefore cannot contain the nonzero-square rank-one Nijenhuis exceptions. The cited primary operator-identity works introduce and compare the identities universally, but do not classify their rank-one solution sets on full matrix algebras or enumerate this boundary. Priority remains bounded by accessible literature.

value.rationale: This is a sharp structural boundary for two central associative operator identities on the natural family of simple full matrix algebras: equality on the full rank-one locus in every matrix size at least three, but a genuinely separate semisimple (scalar-idempotent) operator stratum precisely in size two. The obstruction is a rank inequality for a multiplication bilinear form, not parameter substitution. The exact finite-field exceptional count q^2(q^2-1) and full size-two Nijenhuis count distinguish field-uniform operator geometries and quantify the failure; this is a motivated natural stratum of operator varieties. The result does not claim new general higher-rank structure.
